title: Open redirect sends visitors to any site
summary: A redirect parameter sends the visitor wherever its value points, including an outside site. Attackers use that to make a phishing link look like it belongs to this company, and to steal OAuth tokens by redirecting the sign-in response to a site they control.

confirm.control: A path that cannot exist, so the site's not found answer is known and a real redirect to the foreign host is told apart from it.

reproduce: curl -sk -i 'https://host/?next=https://canary-openredirect.example/' and check the response is a 30x whose Location header points at canary-openredirect.example. Try the other parameter names (url, redirect, return, returnUrl, dest) and the login and logout paths. A path form also works on some servers: curl -sk -i 'https://host/%5Ccanary-openredirect.example/%2f..' answering with Location: /\canary-openredirect.example/..., which a browser reads as the outside host. A redirect to an outside host means the parameter is an open redirect.
remediate: Do not redirect to a location taken from the request. Allow only relative paths, or an explicit allow list of hosts, and reject or ignore an absolute URL to another site.
